## When to apply
Whenever a command, build, or test fails.

## Steps
1. Read the COMPLETE error output, not just the first or last few lines
2. Identify the root cause error - often buried in the middle of cascading failures
3. Distinguish between the primary error and secondary errors caused by it
4. Fix the root cause first, then re-run to see if secondary errors resolve

## Why this matters
The most visible error (usually the last line) is often a symptom, not the cause. A missing header causes dozens of undefined symbol errors - fixing the header fixes all of them. Reading only the tail wastes effort on symptoms.

## Pitfalls
- Reading only the last error and attempting to fix it directly
- Fixing multiple errors at once when they may share a single root cause
- Assuming you know the error without reading the output because a similar command failed before
description: When a command fails, read the COMPLETE error output before attempting fixes.
